subject: english-literature
title: Power & Conflict Poetry Stretch
welcome_lead: Compare like an examiner: how do two poets present power — and how do form and context sharpen the message?
meta_desc: GCSE English Literature — essay-level comparison strategies for the Power and Conflict anthology.
final_note: You practised structured comparison: similar themes, different forms, contrasting contexts, sharper conclusions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A strong thesis says what, how and why.

E.g. 'Both Shelley and Tennyson present rulers as architects of their soldiers' fate, but where Shelley mocks the tyrant, Tennyson glorifies the led.' One sentence — argument for the whole essay.

walkthroughs.h2: Pair poems by argument, not theme
walkthroughs.body_html:
Don't just pick two 'war poems'. Pick poems whose argument contrasts.

Charge of the Light Brigade celebrates obedience ('theirs not to reason why'); Bayonet Charge questions it ('king, honour. luxuries'). The pairing produces tension your essay can explore.

Context should illuminate the poem, not pad the essay.

One sentence is enough: 'Shelley, a radical exile, wrote during a wave of monarchical restoration after Waterloo' — then back to the line analysis.
